MANILA, Philippines – At least three provinces in Northern Luzon are expected to have moderate to heavy rain on Wednesday, October 21, as Super Typhoon Rosal (Champi) accelerated before dawn.
As of 4 am on Wednesday, Rosal was already 990 kilometers east of Northern Luzon, moving west northwest at 30 kilometers per hour from the previous 25 km/h.
The super typhoon had intensified further on Tuesday evening, October 20, with its maximum sustained winds reaching 215 km/h from 195 km/h. Its gustiness also went up to 265 km/h from 240 km/h.

Rosal remains unlikely to make landfall in the Philippines, but it will still have an impact due to its size and intensity. It will be closest to extreme Northern Luzon between Thursday, October 22, and Friday afternoon, October 23.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) released an updated rainfall outlook at 5 am on Wednesday, showing that the following provinces are expected to see significant rain:
Wednesday, October 21

items: Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 millimeters): Ilocos Norte, Apayao, Cagayan

blocks.text: Thursday, October 22

items: Heavy to intense rain (100-200 mm): Batanes
Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Ilocos Norte, Apayao, Cagayan

blocks.text: Friday, October 23

items: Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Batanes

blocks.text: On Wednesday, aside from the provinces mentioned above, Rosal may trigger moderate to at times heavy rain in Batanes, Isabela, and Catanduanes, as well as scattered rain and thunderstorms in the rest of Cagayan Valley, the rest of Bicol, the rest of the Cordillera Administrative Region, Ilocos Sur, Quezon, and Eastern Visayas.
PAGASA also advised more areas to brace for strong winds from the super typhoon. Here are the areas covered by Signal No. 1 as of 5 am on Wednesday:

items: Batanes
Babuyan Islands
mainland Cagayan
eastern part of Isabela (Maconacon, Divilacan, Palanan, Santa Maria, Cabagan, Delfin Albano, Santo Tomas, Tumauini, San Pablo, Ilagan City, San Mariano, Dinapigue)

northeastern part of Catanduanes (Pandan, Bagamanoc, Panganiban, Viga, Gigmoto)

blocks.text: The highest possible tropical cyclone wind signal due to Rosal is Signal No. 2 or 3.
The northeasterly windflow and the periphery or outer bands of the super typhoon will also bring strong to gale-force gusts to the following areas:

items: Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley, Bicol, Romblon, Eastern Visayas, Siquijor, Bohol, Northern Mindanao, Caraga, Davao Region, Sarangani
most of Luzon and Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Northern Mindanao, Agusan del Norte, Surigao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Sarangani, Davao Occidental, Davao Oriental
most of Luzon and Visayas, Camiguin, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental, Davao Oriental

blocks.text: PAGASA said Rosal can still strengthen further as it moves over the Philippine Sea on Wednesday morning, but it is likely to gradually weaken afterwards. It could weaken into a typhoon on Thursday and into a severe tropical storm by Sunday, October 25.
Rosal’s latest forecast track shows it is projected to maintain its west northwest direction on Wednesday, before heading northwest until Friday morning and recurving northeast by Sunday.
It may leave the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by Friday evening or early Saturday morning, October 24.

Rosal, which entered PAR on Tuesday, is the Philippines’ 18th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the first for October. PAGASA earlier estimated the country may have one or two tropical cyclones during the month.
The Philippines is currently in a transition period to the northeast monsoon or amihan, following the end of the southwest monsoon or habagat, which was announced last October 5.

The northeast monsoon typically brings surges of cold temperatures, but the upcoming amihan period could be warmer as the existing strong El Niño in the tropical Pacific Ocean is predicted to become very strong in the fourth quarter of 2026. – Rappler.com
